AbortReason.description: Why the host ended a run (`run_aborted`).

Access.description: What a connection may do in an organization it opens.

Api.description:
An API described by an OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1 document (`archi/04-tools.md`, "API tools"). Each
operation is a tool: its input the path, query and header parameters by name and the JSON
body under `body`; its output the schema of its first `2xx` JSON response.

oneOf.description:
How its calls prove who calls: the document's security requirement when absent. An
`apiKey` in the query or a cookie, or several schemes at once, need it.

baseUrl.description:
Where the calls go: the document's first `servers[]` when absent. `https`, or `http` on
the embedded server.

concurrency.description: Its calls in flight on each worker. 8 by default.

name.description: The namespace of its tools in `rewind:tools`, an identifier as a server's name is.

openapi.description:
Its OpenAPI document in JSON, or the URL it is read from once, at registration (at most
2 MiB, through the egress checks). The document is pinned and never read again.

operations.description:
The `operationId`s to keep, for an API too large for the prompt. Every operation when
absent.

policies.description:
Policies of its tools, by operation name. An operation not listed gets the default of
its method: `retry` for `GET`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`, `PUT` and `DELETE`; `at_most_once`
for `POST` and `PATCH` unless it declares an `Idempotency-Key` header.

ApiKey.description: An API key, without its secret but in the answer to its creation.

allowedLabels.description: The allowed labels of the key's grant.

createdBy.description:
The principal who created it: `user:<id>` or `key:<id>`. Absent for the operator's key
given at start.

id.description: For `DELETE /v1/api-keys/{id}`: the hex of the key's SHA-256. Not a secret.

key.description:
The key, `rewind_sk_…`, to send as `Authorization: Bearer rewind_sk_…`. Only in the answer
to `POST /v1/api-keys`.

role.description: The role of the key's grant.

ApiKeyList.description: `GET /v1/api-keys`: the tenant's keys, revoked ones included, oldest first.

ApiSummary.description: An API of a toolset, as pinned.

oneOf.description: How its calls authenticate; absent for none.

AttachmentProblem.description:
One attachment that refused a start, a fork or a save, with what the caller may attach for
that server instead.

attachable.description: The secrets the caller may attach for that server, `org/<name>` and `ns/<name>`.

secret.description: The secret attached, as the request named it.

AttachmentProblemKind.description: Why an attachment refused a start, a fork or a save (`secret-required`).

Auth.description:
How the calls to an MCP server or an API prove who calls (`archi/04-tools.md`,
"Authenticating calls"). Part of the pinned toolset; never a value.

oneOf.description:
Nothing: a public server. For an API, overrides its document's security requirement.
(A struct variant, so that unknown fields are refused.)

A JWT signed with the organization's key, in `Authorization: Bearer`: the customer's own
servers check it (`verifyRewindCall`) and learn the end user from `sub`. HTTP servers
and APIs.

The secret the run attached for the server: in `header` (with `format`, `{secret}`
replaced by its value, and `encoding`), or in the variable `env` of a stdio server.
Exactly one of `header` and `env`.
`base64` writes the secret in base64 into `format` (HTTP basic: `user:password`).

AuthConfig.description: `GET /auth/config`: how to sign in on this server.

waitlist.description:
Sign-ups are closed: someone without an account nor an invitation joins the waitlist
(`POST /auth/waitlist`).

oneOf.description: Signed in: send the access token to `/v1` as a Bearer token, and keep it in memory only.

expiresAt.description:
Ask `POST /auth/session` again before then: it refreshes a token with less than a
minute left.

organizationId.description:
The organization of the session, the tenant `/v1` acts in. Absent without one:
create one, or accept an invitation.

oneOf.description: The user belongs to several organizations: choose one with `POST /auth/organization`.
A code was sent to the email: give it to `POST /auth/email-verification`.

Sign-ups are closed and this person has no account nor invitation: they may join the
waitlist.

client_id_metadata_document_supported.description: A `client_id` may be the `https` URL of the client's metadata document.

CallAttempts.description: How many times a tool call was sent.

Callsite.description: A position in the script's TypeScript source (`script.ts`), 1-based.

CancelReason.description: Why a run is being cancelled.

CancelRun.description:
`POST /v1/runs/{id}/cancel`: every pending await of the script rejects with
`CancelledError`; the script gets one activation to clean up.

oneOf.description:
Hold the answer until the run ends or is quarantined, or until this long has passed, as
`POST /v1/runs` does.

ChangeEvent.description:
One event of the change stream (`GET /v1/changes`). On the wire, each is a server-sent event
whose `event` field names it and whose `data` is this JSON value: for `run`, the run's
summary, the very object `GET /v1/runs` lists, pushed by the run's owner once its batch is
durable; for `script`, `workflow`, `secret`, `namespace` and `connection`, what changed in the
control plane, by its name or id (the client reads again the views that show it); for
`resync`, `{}`. Each reaches the caller only if it may see what changed. Events have no `id`:
the stream is not resumed, the client reads again what it shows. While it sends nothing else,
the server writes a comment line (`:`) at least every 15 seconds.

oneOf.description: `run`: a run changed. Its summary as it is now, as `GET /v1/runs` lists it.
`script`: the organization's runs ran a script for the first time.
`workflow`: a workflow has a new version.
`secret`: a secret was put or deleted.

`namespace`: a namespace was created, renamed, given other limits or tokens, or erased;
or the organization's default limits or ceiling changed.
`connection`: a connection was made, changed, used or revoked.

`resync`: more changed at once than the server reads in one pass. Read again what is
shown.

CheckRequest.description:
`POST /v1/check`: type-checks a script against the sandbox lib and a toolset's
declarations, in strict mode, before anything runs.

script.description: The TypeScript source: a single ES module whose default export is the entry point.

toolset.description: The toolset whose `rewind:tools` the script imports. Without one, `rewind:tools` is empty.

CheckResult.description: The diagnostics of a check. A script with only warnings passes.

ClientKind.description: How a client made itself known to Rewind.

ClientMetadata.description:
A client's metadata: the body of `POST /oauth/register` (RFC 7591), and a client's metadata
document, whose `client_id` is its own URL. Other fields are ignored.

client_id.description: A metadata document's own URL; none at registration.

redirect_uris.description:
Each `https`, `http` on a loopback address, or a private-use scheme holding a dot
(`cursor://…`).

token_endpoint_auth_method.description:
`none`, `client_secret_post` or `client_secret_basic` (RFC 7591's default) at
registration; `none` in a metadata document.

CompleteTask.description: `POST /v1/tasks/{token}/complete`: the tool's result, delivered to the script.

lastUsedAt.description: When an access token of it was last used, to the minute.

organizations.description:
The organizations it opens, by id. `GET /v1/organization/connections` gives the
caller's organization only.

ConnectionChanged.description:
The data of a `connection` event: one of the caller's own connections, or a connection that
opens the organization, was made, changed, revoked or taken out of the organization, or its
`lastUsedAt` moved.

ConnectionClient.description: The client a connection was made through.

id.description: The URL of its metadata document, or `rc_…`.

ConnectionList.description:
`GET /v1/connections` (the caller's) and `GET /v1/organization/connections` (those that open
the organization).

allowedLabels.description:
The labels of the connection's grant there: what it starts carries them, and it sees
only the runs carrying them.

name.description: Its name; unknown on a server without the identity provider.

email.description: Unknown on a server without the identity provider.

allowedLabels.description: The labels proposed for the connection's grants: what it starts carries them.

expiresAt.description: When the request lapses: the client starts again after.

loopback.description:
The client returns to a loopback address: a program on the person's machine, which the
page warns about.

redirectHost.description: The host the browser returns to with the code.

allowedLabels.description: The labels of the connection's grants.

organizations.description: For `allow`: at least one organization, each where the person's grant gives its access.

ConsentChoice.description: An organization ticked at consent, with its access.

ConsentClient.description: The client asking for a connection.

ConsentOrganization.description: One of the person's organizations, as the consent offers it.

accesses.description:
The accesses the person may give there: those whose permissions their grant holds.
Empty: they cannot open it.

current.description: The organization of the caller's access token: ticked in advance.

role.description: The role of the person's grant there; none without a grant.

ConsentRedirect.description:
Where the consent page sends the browser: the client's redirect URI, with the code and the
state, or with `error=access_denied`.

CreateApiKey.description:
`POST /v1/api-keys`: a key `rewind_sk_…`, with its grant. Keys are stored hashed: the key
itself is only in the answer. Creating a key needs every permission of its role.

allowedLabels.description:
The key only sees runs carrying all these labels: an agent's tools see only their own
conversation's runs.

role.description: A built-in role, a role of the tenant, or `operator` (only from the operator).

tenant.description:
Another tenant than the caller's: only the operator names one, and the tenant is
created with its first key.

CreateInvitation.description:
`POST /v1/organization/invitations`: invites an email with a role and allowed labels.
Inviting needs every permission of the role given.

CreateOrganization.description: `POST /v1/organizations`: a new organization, whose creator is its `owner`.

events.description: The events to send. Every event when empty.

labels.description:
Only events about runs carrying these labels. A key limited to labels can only
subscribe within them.

url.description: An HTTPS URL of the harness.

labels.description: The runs the token reaches carry all of these labels, and the runs it starts get them.

permissions.description:
Among [`Permission::TOKEN`], each held by the caller; [`Permission::TOKEN_DEFAULT`]
when absent.

oneOf.description: How long the token lives: 1 hour by default, 30 days at most.

CreateTokenKey.description: `POST /v1/organization/token-keys`: a public key the customer signs end users' tokens with.

jwk.description:
The public key as a JWK (RFC 7517): `OKP` with `crv` `Ed25519`, `EC` with `crv` `P-256`,
or `RSA` of at least 2048 bits. A private part is refused.

permissions.description:
The permissions its tokens may carry, among [`Permission::TOKEN`] and held by the caller;
all of those the caller holds when absent.

CreateToolset.description:
`POST /v1/toolsets`: MCP servers, APIs, host tools and the `http` tool, with a policy per
tool. Registering connects to the MCP servers and lists their tools, reads the APIs' OpenAPI
documents, and pins their schemas. The toolset is content-addressed: registering the same
toolset twice gives the same id. It holds no secret: a run attaches its secrets when it
starts.

host.description: Ask the end user a question and return their answer.
host.name: ask_user

apis.description:
APIs described by OpenAPI documents: one tool per operation, named
`<api>.<operationId>`, called by Rewind.

base.description:
Derives the toolset from a registered one: its servers, tools and workflows are kept as
pinned, without listing the servers again; `workflows` adds workflows or pins them again.
`mcp`, `host` and `http` must then be empty.

host.description:
Host tools: functions of the harness, executed by its SDK worker (`GET /v1/tasks`). A
name `group.tool` puts the tool in the `group` namespace of `rewind:tools`.

oneOf.description: Enables the built-in `http` tool, and `fetch` in scripts, for these hosts only.

mcp.description: MCP servers. Their tools are called by Rewind and named `<server>.<tool>`.

secrets.description:
The organization's secrets that list the tools of the MCP servers whose `auth` takes one,
by server: `{ "github": "org/github" }`. Only `org/` secrets; no run keeps them, and they
are not part of the toolset's id. Requires `secrets:use`.

workflows.description:
The workflows its scripts may start, from `rewind:workflows`: `triage` pins the latest
version, `triage@<version>` or `triage@v12` one version. The versions are pinned: the
toolset's scripts are checked against them, and start them, for their whole life.

CreateWorkflow.description:
`POST /v1/workflows`: checks a workflow and saves it as a new version. Its script is checked
against its toolset and against its own schemas: its default export must take the input and
return the output, and `signal()` only takes the declared names. Saving the same workflow
again under the same labels returns the version saved first (200): the labels of a key limited
to labels are part of the version, so such a key saves a version of its own.

example.description: Triage the stale issues of a repository, after approval.
example.name: triage

description.description: Shown to the model in the declarations.

input.description: JSON Schema of the input of `main`.

name.description:
What scripts import from `rewind:workflows`: an identifier that is not a reserved word of
JavaScript.

parent.description:
The version it derives from, `name@<version>`, `name@v<number>` or a version: the latest
version of the same name saved under the caller's labels when absent. Its suite is
inherited.

retire.description: Inherited tests dropped, with a reason: they are deprecated.

script.description: The TypeScript source: a single ES module whose default export is the entry point.

secrets.description:
The secrets its runs attach, by MCP server or API (`org/<name>`, `ns/<name>`), part of
the version: checked against the saver's rights now (an `ns/` secret by its name only),
and read by its runs without checking the caller's again (`secret-required`).

signals.description:
The signals its runs accept, by name, each with the JSON Schema of its payload. Names
starting with `rewind:` are reserved.

tests.description:
New tests: inline, by the digest of a recorded test, or a recorded test with a new
expectation.

toolset.description: The id of the toolset its runs call, already registered.

update.description: Inherited tests replaced, each with a reason: their state or result is out of date.

CredentialsExpired.description:
A call parked because its server refused the secret or the signature (`refused`), or
because the secret the run attached no longer exists (`missing`, nothing was sent). Put the
secret again (`PUT /v1/secrets/{name}`, `PUT /v1/namespaces/{name}/secrets/{secret}`), or,
for a refused signature, approve the call once the server accepts the key: the call is then
sent again with the same idempotency key.

message.description: What the server answered, or which secret is missing.

secret.description:
The secret the run attached for the server, as attached (`org/<name>`, `ns/<name>`);
absent for a signed call.

server.description: The tool's MCP server or API.

DailyReads.description: The reads of a secret on one day (UTC).

dts.description:
`rewind-tools.d.ts`: the `rewind:tools` module, with tool descriptions as JSDoc, and the
`rewind:workflows` module when the toolset pins workflows.

prompt.description: The compact rendering for the model's prompt, one line per tool.

DeferTask.description:
`POST /v1/tasks/{token}/defer`: the handler will answer later, possibly days later, with
`/complete` or `/fail` and the same token, whether the task stream it was handed on stays open
or not: its slot on the stream is free.

oneOf.description:
Fail the call with `timeout` if no answer comes within this time. Bounded by the run's
TTL, which is the default.

Diagnostic.description:
One finding of the checks: tsgo's type errors, the checks at start, and the checker's own
rules. Written for a model.

example.message: Type 'number' is not assignable to type 'string'.

code.description:
`TS<n>` for tsgo; `rewind/<rule>` for the checks at start and the checker's own rules
(`rewind/floating-promise`, `rewind/ignored-async-callback`, `rewind/absent-global`…).

frame.description: A few lines of the source around the location, with the span underlined.

hint.description: What to do instead, when the checker knows (the hint of an absent global, for example).

oneOf.description: Where in `script.ts`; absent for a diagnostic about the script as a whole.

Duration.description: A duration: a number and a unit (ms, s, m, h, d, w), possibly several ("1h30m"), or a number of milliseconds.

oneOf.description: milliseconds

EmailVerification.description:
`POST /auth/email-verification`: the code sent to verify the email, after
`email_verification_required`.

idx.description: Position in the history: from 0, contiguous.

recordedAt.description:
When the entry was committed; monotonic per run. Once a trigger is delivered, it is the
script's logical time.

Event.description: A journal event (`archi/02-journal.md`): lifecycle, commands, completions and annotations.

oneOf.description: The run's first entry. The seed is left out: it is only in the exported journal.
The host ended the run.
The script started waiting for a signal whose mailbox was empty.

timeout.description: The `seq` of the timer of its timeout.

Expectations.description: What must hold at the end of a test. Everything not given is not checked.

calls.description:
Calls that must happen: those to `tool` whose args contain `args`, exactly `times` of
them, at least one when `times` is absent; `times: 0` forbids them. Calls the world
answers that are not listed are allowed.

oneOf.description: The run failed with an error of this name, whose message contains `message`.
`listed`: the first call matching each entry comes in the order of the entries.

output.description: The output contains these values (objects are compared key by key, recursively).

oneOf.description: `active` for a run that can go no further in virtual time without the outside world.

Facets.description:
The most frequent values among the runs, most frequent first: what to suggest in a query
bar, and the counts beside a list. The counters count the runs of the window by status, by
workflow and by namespace; the facets they do not count are empty.

errors.description: Errors the runs ended with (names and abort kinds), and kinds their calls failed with.

labels.description: The most frequent label keys, each with its most frequent values.

namespaces.description: Namespaces, for a reader of every namespace; a reader of one sees only its own.

workflows.description: Workflows, by name: the runs of each.

FailTask.description:
`POST /v1/tasks/{token}/fail`: the tool failed. The script gets a `ToolError`, unless the
failure is retryable and the tool's policy is `retry`: the call is then made again, with
backoff.

message.description: The message of the `ToolError`, written for the model.

retryable.description: A transient failure: call again later.

FailureGroup.description:
The runs that ended the same way: the same error name, and the same message once numbers,
ids, times and double-quoted strings are set aside.

error.description: The error's name, or the abort's kind.

labels.description: Its runs' most frequent labels, as `key:value`.

line.description: The line of `script.ts` most of its runs ended at.

series.description: One count per bucket from `since`: the runs that ended in it.

signature.description:
The error's name and message with placeholders (`<n>`, `<id>`, `<uuid>`, `<time>`,
`<str>`) where they vary.

groups.description: The most runs first, then the latest ending first.

ForkParent.description: The run a fork was started from.

at.description: The entry from which the fork was forced live, if the request gave one.

handle.description: The parent's handle; its id once it is erased.

ForkRun.description:
`POST /v1/runs/{id}/fork` (`retry_run`): a new run with a corrected script. While its
commands match the parent's, the parent's recorded results are reused and no tool is called
again; it continues live at the first difference, at `at`, or at the end of the parent's
history (`archi/03-execution.md`, "Forks"). Takes `Idempotency-Key` as `POST /v1/runs`.

at.description: Go live from this journal entry even if the commands still match.

check.description: Type-check the corrected script first. `true` by default.

input.description: The fork's input. The parent's when absent.

oneOf.description:
The fork's labels. Absent, the fork keeps its parent's labels, so that whoever sees the
parent (the agent tools of a conversation, a key limited to labels) sees the fork.

The fork's attachments, as `POST /v1/runs` takes them. The parent's when absent. Either
way they are checked against the caller: the script is new code.
A new TTL, from the fork's start. 30 days by default.

Hold the answer until the fork ends or is quarantined, or until this long has passed, as
`POST /v1/runs` does.

Grant.description: What a principal holds in a tenant: a role, and optionally allowed labels.

allowedLabels.description: The principal only sees the runs carrying all these labels, and cannot administer.

grantedBy.description:
The principal who gave it: `user:<id>` or `key:<id>`. Absent for the grants the server
gives (an organization's creator, a member's default role, the operator).

role.description:
A built-in role, an organization's own, or `operator`. A grant whose role no longer
exists gives no permission.

HandedTask.description:
A host-tool call handed to a worker on its task stream. The worker answers it by its token,
with `/complete` or `/fail`, or `/defer` to answer later; nothing else is asked of it while it
works.

args.description: The arguments, validated against the tool's input schema.

attempt.description:
From 1. Above 1, an earlier attempt was interrupted: the stream it was handed on closed
and did not come back within its grace.

id.description: The task's id, as listed in the run's state.

idempotencyKey.description:
`{run_id}/{seq}` (a fork's call made again keeps its parent's), the same on every
attempt: the handler uses it to recognize a call it already made.

namespace.description: The namespace of the run: the end user the handler acts for.

timeoutMs.description:
The tool's execution timeout, in milliseconds: past it, the call is not waited for any
more. Absent when the tool has none, the default of host tools: the run's TTL bounds it.

token.description:
The hand-out's secret token: `/v1/tasks/{token}/…`. A new one at each hand-out. It names
the run, so an answer reaches the run's owner from whichever process receives it.

traceparent.description: W3C trace context, with the tool call's span as parent.

HostTool.description: A function of the harness, called by scripts and executed by the harness's SDK worker.

description.description: Shown to the model in the declarations.

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema of the arguments. Arguments are validated against it before the call.

name.description:
`group.tool` puts the tool in a group, the namespace `rewind:tools` exports it under. The
group, and a name without a dot, may not be a reserved word of JavaScript.

outputSchema.description: JSON Schema of the result, for the declarations. Results are not validated.

HttpTool.description:
The built-in `http` tool: requests leave from the dispatcher, never from the isolate, and
only toward these hosts (`archi/04-tools.md`, "The `http` tool and egress").

allow.description: Host names, such as `api.example.com`. `*.example.com` allows the subdomains.

Identity.description:
`GET /v1/whoami`: who calls, and what they may do. Over the embedded server's socket, which
takes no token: the operator of the tenant `local`.

oneOf.description:
The caller's grant in the tenant. Absent for a member without one, who gets 403 on the
tenant's data.

operator.description: The deployment's operator: every permission in its tenant, and the keys of every tenant.

oneOf.description: For a member: the organization of the session.

organizations.description: For a member: every organization they belong to.

permissions.description: What the grant's role allows, in the catalog's order.

oneOf.description: Absent over the embedded server's socket.

tenant.description:
The tenant the caller acts in. Absent for a member signed in without an organization,
who reaches only the onboarding endpoints.

Invitation.description: An invitation sent by email, with the grant its invitee gets on accepting it.

oneOf.description: The pending grant, which becomes the invitee's when they accept.

inviter.description: The id of the member who invited.

oneOf.description: The organization it invites to.

x.description: The public key, in base64url without padding.

Jwks.description:
`GET /organizations/{tenant}/jwks.json`: the organization's public keys, as a JSON Web Key
Set (RFC 7517), served without authentication.

Labels.description:
Run labels: a bounded string map set when a run starts (agent, conversation, end user…).
They filter runs and scope API keys and webhooks. The script never sees them.

LastRead.description:
The last read of a secret: by which run, of which namespace, when. A toolset's registration
reads an organization's secret to list the tools of the MCP server it is attached for, before
any run exists: such a read names neither run nor namespace.

oneOf.description: The namespace of that run; `null` for a toolset's registration.

run.description: The run that read it; `null` for a toolset's registration.

runHandle.description: That run's handle, while the run is kept.

Location.description: A span in `script.ts`, 1-based, the end exclusive.

LogLine.description: One line of the script's console.

MagicAuthRequest.description: `POST /auth/magic-auth`: sends a 6-digit code to the email.

invitationToken.description: The token of the invitation the page was opened with.

McpServer.description:
An MCP server: exactly one of `url` (streamable HTTP) and `command` (stdio).

A server of a deployment refuses `command` unless its configuration allows it: a stdio
server is a process started by Rewind. The embedded server accepts it.

oneOf.description: How its calls prove who calls. None when absent.

command.description: The program of a stdio server.

env.description:
Environment of a stdio server that is not secret. A secret goes in the variable its
`auth` names.

name.description:
The namespace of its tools in `rewind:tools`: an identifier that is not a reserved word of
JavaScript (`default`, `delete`, `let`…).

policies.description:
Policies of its tools, by tool name as the server defines it. Tools not listed get the
default policy.

url.description:
The URL of a streamable HTTP server. A server of a deployment reaches it only at a public
address, unless its configuration allows the internal host.

Member.description: A member of the organization, with their grant.

oneOf.description:
Absent for a member without a grant: one who has not had a session in the organization
yet, or whose grant was removed.

Namespace.description: A namespace with its limits and its use of a month.

deletingSince.description: Set while the namespace is being erased: it takes no run and no token.

displayName.description: The customer's label for the end user, shown beside the name, which stays its key.

exceptions.description: The namespace's exceptions to the defaults.

lastActiveAt.description: The last run created in it, or the last CPU time counted for it.

limits.description: The limits that apply: per quota, the namespace's exception, else the tenant's default.

usage.description: Its use of the month listed.

NamespaceChanged.description:
The data of a `namespace` event: a namespace created, renamed, given other exceptions or
tokens, or being erased or erased; without `name`, the organization's default limits or its
ceiling, which every namespace's limits follow.

NamespaceDefaults.description:
`GET /v1/organization/namespace-defaults`: the limits of every namespace without an
exception, and the tenant's ceiling with its use of the month.

ceiling.description: Set by the operator: the customer's offer, on its totals across namespaces.

usage.description: The tenant's use of the month, across its namespaces.

NamespaceDetail.description: `GET /v1/namespaces/{name}`: one namespace, its use day by day, its alerts and its tokens.

days.description: The days of the month with some use, oldest first.

tokens.description: Opaque tokens of the namespace neither revoked nor expired.

tokensRevokedBefore.description: Signed tokens issued before this are refused.

month.description: The month whose use is listed, `2026-11`.

next.description: The cursor of the next page, absent on the last one.

total.description: How many namespaces match the query, across every page.

NamespaceName.description:
A namespace's name: the customer's own id for the end user. 1 to 128 ASCII letters, digits,
`-`, `_`, `.`, `:` and `@`, case-sensitive. `*` is not a name: it stands for the tenant in
the store's usage and alerts.

NamespaceNames.description:
`GET /v1/organization/namespace-names`: every namespace of the organization that has a
display name, by name. Not paged.

NamespacePatch.description:
`PATCH /v1/namespaces/{name}`: a JSON merge patch (RFC 7396) of the namespace, which must
exist. What is absent stays.

OAuthError.description:
An OAuth error (RFC 6749, section 5.2; RFC 7591, section 3.2.2), answered as
`application/json` with `Cache-Control: no-store`.

OnInterruption.description: After an interruption (the dispatcher or the worker died mid-call).

OpenApiDocument.description: An OpenAPI document, or where to read it.

oneOf.description: Its URL.
The document itself, in JSON.

OpenOrganization.description: An organization to open, with its access and labels.

Organization.description: An organization: a tenant, with the same id.

OrganizationSettings.description: The organization of the caller's session, with its settings.

defaultRole.description: The role a member gets at their first session, without an invitation's grant.

Payload.description:
A JSON value carried by a run (its input and output, tool arguments and results, signal
payloads), identified by the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON (RFC 8785).

bytes.description: Size of the canonical JSON, in bytes.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON, lowercase hex.

preview.description: The start of the canonical JSON, for display.

value.description:
The value itself. Left out when it is larger than the endpoint returns inline
(`PAYLOAD_VALUE_LIMIT`, 256 KiB): read it with `GET /v1/payloads/{digest}`.

Permission.description: A kind of action. Every endpoint requires one; a role is a set of them.

PermissionInfo.description: A permission of the catalog, with what it lets the caller do.

oneOf.description: An API key.
A member, signed in on the dashboard.
An end user's token: it reaches its namespace only, with its own permissions.

id.description: For an opaque token: its id (`DELETE /v1/tokens/{id}`).

kid.description: For a signed token: the key that signed it, and its `jti` if it has one.

oneOf.description:
A person's connection (`rewind_ct_…`): an MCP client acting for the person, in the
organizations it opens. With `Rewind-Organization`, the identity's tenant, grant and
permissions are the connection's there.

organizations.description: The organizations it opens, with their access and labels.

allOf.description: With `quota-exceeded`: the quota reached, its scope, its limit, what is used, and when a monthly quota frees.

attachments.description: With `secret-required`: each attachment at fault, with what the caller may attach.

detail.description: What went wrong in this request, and what to do instead. Written for a model.

diagnostics.description: With `invalid-script`: why the script was refused, with locations in `script.ts`.

instance.description: The path of the request, or of the resource the problem is about.

oneOf.description: With `invalid-query`: where the term at fault is in the query.

tests.description:
With `tests-failed`: every test of the run, those that did not pass with their problem
and failures.

title.description: A short summary of the kind of problem, the same for every occurrence.

Problem.description: An error answered by the API, as `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457).

example.detail: run 0193a5c4-7d2e-7c1a-9b1e-3f6a2d9c8e10 has ended (completed): a signal can only be sent to a run that is still active
example.title: The run has ended

PutCeiling.description: `PUT /v1/organizations/{tenant}/quotas`: the operator replaces a tenant's ceiling.

PutNamespace.description:
`PUT /v1/namespaces/{name}`: creates the namespace, or replaces its exceptions. A quota
absent from `exceptions` follows the tenant's default.

PutRole.description:
`PUT /v1/roles/{name}`: creates or changes a role of the organization. Writing a role needs
every permission it gives. A change applies at once to every principal holding the role.

PutSecret.description:
`PUT /v1/secrets/{name}` and `PUT /v1/namespaces/{name}/secrets/{secret}`: creates or
replaces a secret. Replacing it makes ready the calls a refusal or a missing secret parked in
the runs that attach it, sent again with the same idempotency key.

labels.description:
An organization's secret's labels: a grant limited to labels sees, writes and attaches
only the secrets carrying them, and the secrets it writes take them. A namespace's secret
takes none (`invalid-request`).

value.description: The value: a string of at most 16 KiB. Written, never read back.

Quarantine.description: Why a run is quarantined (`archi/03-execution.md`, "Non-determinism and quarantine").

reason.description: The replay mismatch, or the last error.

QuerySpan.description: A position in a query, in characters (Unicode scalar values) from 0, `end` excluded.

QuotaAlert.description: A limit crossed: sent once as the webhook `quota.alert`, and listed by the API.

limit.description: The limit, in the same unit.

oneOf.description: The namespace; absent (`null` in the webhook) for the tenant's ceiling.

sentAt.description: When it was delivered to the tenant's subscriptions.

threshold.description:
80 or 100: the share of the limit crossed; for `active_runs`, 100 at the first refusal
of the month.

used.description: The use when the alert was raised: milliseconds for `cpu_per_month`, a count otherwise.

QuotaAlertList.description: `GET /v1/organization/quota-alerts`: the alerts of a month, newest first.

QuotaKind.description: A quota, as `quota-exceeded` and `quota.alert` name it.

QuotaReached.description:
The quota a `quota-exceeded` problem reached. A monthly quota's answer also carries
`Retry-After`.

limit.description: The limit: a count for `active_runs`, `runs_per_month` and `scripts`.

resetsAt.description:
When a monthly quota frees: the first instant of the next month (UTC). Absent for
`active_runs` and `scripts`, which free when runs end or are erased.

QuotaScope.description:
Which limit a quota belongs to: the namespace's (its exception, else the default), or the
tenant's ceiling.

QuotaUsage.description: What a namespace, or the tenant, used in a calendar month.

cpu.description: CPU time of the month, replays excluded.

runsStarted.description: Runs created in the month, forks included.

scripts.description: Distinct scripts with at least one run kept.

Quotas.description:
Limits, each optional: an absent one does not limit. The same shape serves a tenant's
defaults for every namespace, a namespace's exceptions, the limits that apply to a
namespace, and the tenant's ceiling, which bounds its totals.

activeRuns.description: Runs active at once. Starting or forking one more is refused (429).

oneOf.description:
CPU time of the isolates running the namespace's scripts in a calendar month (UTC),
replays excluded. Never refused: crossing 80 % and 100 % sends `quota.alert`.

maxScriptLines.description: The most lines a script may have (422 `invalid-script` above it).

oneOf.description: The longest TTL a run may ask for; the default TTL is lowered to it (400 above it).

runsPerMonth.description: Runs created in a calendar month, forks included (429 above it).

scripts.description:
Distinct scripts with at least one run kept in the namespace (429 for a new one above
it).

RecordTests.description:
`POST /v1/workflows/{name}/record`: tests recorded from the workflow's past runs, one per
path. They are stored, and join a suite only when a save references them.

limit.description: At most this many tests: 20 by default, 100 at most.

query.description:
Which runs, in the query language of the run lists; the completed and failed runs of the
workflow, newest first, the 1,000 newest at most.

runs.description: These runs, rather than a query.

RecordedTest.description: A test recorded from a run.

path.description:
The path the run took: `github.list_issues · signal approval · github.close_issue×n →
completed`.

skipped.description: The runs left out, and why.

RegisteredClient.description:
`POST /oauth/register`'s answer (RFC 7591): the client, with its secret for a confidential
one, shown only here.

RejectTask.description: `POST /v1/tasks/{id}/reject`: the call fails with a `ToolError` carrying this message.

message.description: Why, written for the model. "rejected by the harness" when absent.

Resync.description: The data of a `resync` event: an empty object.

RetiredTest.description: A test of the parent a version does not keep.

revokedBefore.description: Signed tokens issued before this are refused.

Role.description: A role: one of the four built-in roles, or the organization's own.

builtIn.description: A built-in role, which never changes.

RoleList.description: `GET /v1/roles`: the built-in roles, then the organization's own, by name.

RuleError.description: A failure a rule answers with.

oneOf.description: `error` when absent.

Run.description: The state of a run: a projection of its journal, with its metadata.

oneOf.description: With `aborted`: why the host ended the run.

attempts.description:
How many times each tool call was sent, by seq, for the calls sent more than once: a
call retried after a transient failure, or sent again after its worker or dispatcher
died. Attempts live in the tool tasks, not in the journal: the read model keeps them.

epoch.description: The determinism epoch the run started under.

oneOf.description: With `failed` or `cancelled`: how the script failed.

expiresAt.description: The deadline: the run is cancelled then (reason `ttl`).

handle.description:
The run's handle, `<namespace>/<origin>/<suffix>`: what people read, copy and type to
name it. Every path and query parameter that takes a run's id takes its handle too,
percent-encoded in a path (`dana%2Ftriage%2F06bqx3k9f2mt`).

oneOf.description:
The input of `main`. Absent while the run is `pending`: its `run_started` waits in its
inbox for the first activation, which commits it.

logs.description: The last log lines of the script (`console.*`), oldest first, at most 20.

namespace.description: The end user the run belongs to. A fork has its parent's.

oneOf.description: With `completed`: what `main` returned.
For a fork, the run it was forked from.

Set while the run is quarantined: its activations are stopped until it is released or
given up. Quarantine is not a status.

scriptTitle.description:
The script's title: the one a person gave it (`PATCH /v1/scripts/{digest}`), else the
first line of the comment at its top. Absent when it has neither.

secrets.description:
The secrets it attached at start, by MCP server or API (`org/<name>`, `ns/<name>`):
names, never values.

oneOf.description: For a run a script started, that run and the call.

traceId.description:
The OpenTelemetry trace the run belongs to: the caller's if it gave a `traceparent`,
else derived from the run id. 32 hex digits.

waitingFor.description: With `active`: what the run waits for.

oneOf.description: For a run of a workflow, the workflow and its version.

RunCounts.description: A number of runs per status.

RunError.description: How a script failed, with where, for a model to fix it.

oneOf.description: The tool call whose failure the script did not catch, if that is how it failed.

frame.description: A few lines of the source around `location`.

oneOf.description: The innermost frame of the stack in `script.ts`.

stack.description: Source-mapped to `script.ts`, without the runtime's frames.

RunEvent.description: The run an event is about, in the state the event left it in.

RunMode.description:
`live`: tools are really called and time is real. `mock`: tools are answered by cassettes
and mocks, and time is virtual.

RunPage.description:
A page of runs. It may hold fewer runs than `limit`, possibly none, and still have a
`nextCursor`: the server stopped at its scan budget. Only a page without `nextCursor` is the
last.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` to read the next page; absent on the last page only.

RunStats.description:
The runs of a scope. Counts, series, durations and facets are over the runs started in the
window, from the hourly counters; `since`, `until` and `bucket` are the window and the width
the answer used, in whole hours. `waiting` and `quarantined` are over the active runs of the
scope now, whenever they started, from the gauge of the active runs.

bucket.description: The width of the series' buckets, if any.

oneOf.description: From start to end, in milliseconds, over the runs that ended.

series.description: One bucket per `bucket` from `since`, the runs started in it by status.

waiting.description: Waiting runs by what they wait for; a run waiting for several kinds counts in each.

RunStatus.description:
The status of a run, a function of its journal (`archi/02-journal.md`, "Run state").
Quarantine is not a status: see `Run.quarantine`.

RunSummary.description: A run in a list, from the read model.

error.description: With `failed` or `cancelled`: the error's name. With `aborted`: the abort's kind.

errorLine.description: With `error`: the innermost line of `script.ts` in the error's stack, if any.

errorMessage.description: With `error`: the error's or the abort's message.

fingerprint.description: With `error`: the failure group (`GET /v1/runs/failures`, `fingerprint:` in a query).

headline.description: The first line of the script that is not blank, for display.

scriptTitle.description: The script's title, as `Run.scriptTitle`. Absent when it has none.

startedBy.description: For a run a script started, that run.

waitingFor.description: With `active`: what the run waits for.

wakesAt.description: With `active`: when the run wakes by itself, if a timer or a signal's timeout wakes it.

workflow.description: For a run of a workflow, the workflow's name.

RunWait.description: Something a run in a list waits for. `GET /v1/runs/{id}` has the details (`waitingFor`).

name.description: The signal's name, or the call's tool.

seq.description: The timer's or the call's seq.

until.description: When the wait ends by itself: a timer's due time, a signal's timeout.

number.description: The version's number among the versions of its workflow (`Workflow.number`).

Script.description: `GET /v1/scripts/{digest}`: one script's source, and what its runs did.

firstRunAt.description: When its first and last runs started; absent when no run is kept.

headline.description: The first line of the source that is not blank, for display.

runs.description: Runs of this script, by status, as the read model keeps them.

oneOf.description: Where the title comes from; absent without a title.

ScriptChanged.description:
The data of a `script` event: a script the organization's runs ran for the first time, which
`GET /v1/scripts` now lists.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the TypeScript source, lowercase hex.

ScriptError.description:
How a script failed: what `main` threw, the rejection it left unhandled, `DeadlockError`,
or `CancelledError`.

stack.description: The stack, source-mapped to `script.ts`, without the runtime's own frames.

nextCursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` to read the next page; absent on the last page.

ScriptSummary.description: A distinct script: content-addressed, so every run of the same source counts here.

description.description:
The description that goes with the title: the person's with theirs, else the rest of
the comment.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the TypeScript source, lowercase hex.

headline.description: The first line of the source that is not blank, for display.

runs.description: Runs of this script, by status.

title.description:
The script's title: the one a person gave it, else the first line of the comment at its
top. Absent when it has neither.

oneOf.description: Where the title comes from; absent without a title.

Secret.description: A secret, as listed: its metadata, never its value.

createdBy.description:
Who wrote it first: a principal (`user:…`, `key:…`, `connection:…`) or an end user's
token (`token:<namespace>`).

labels.description: An organization's secret's labels; none for a namespace's.

oneOf.description: Its last read, if it was ever read.

name.description: 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`, starting with a letter.

oneOf.description: A namespace's secret's namespace.

reads.description: Its reads per day over the last 30 days, oldest first; a day without a read is left out.

SecretChanged.description: The data of a `secret` event: a secret put (created or given a new value) or deleted.

oneOf.description: The namespace whose secret it is; absent for the organization's.

SecretEncoding.description: How a secret is written into a header's `format`.

SecretList.description:
`GET /v1/secrets`, `GET /v1/namespaces/{name}/secrets`: the secrets the caller sees, sorted
by name.

SecretUsage.description:
`GET /v1/secrets/{name}/usage`, `GET /v1/namespaces/{name}/secrets/{secret}/usage`: what
reads a secret, what deleting it would stop.

activeRuns.description: The active runs that attach it, oldest first, at most 100.

activeTotal.description: How many active runs attach it.

secret.description: The secret, with its reads and its last read.

waitingRuns.description:
Those of them with a call to a server it serves that is parked or not yet sent, at most
100.

workflows.description:
The workflows whose latest version attaches it. A version attaching `ns/<name>` counts
for the secret `<name>` of every namespace.

ServerInfo.description:
`GET /v1/server`: what this server is. Every response also carries the `Rewind-Version`
header.

embedded.description: `rewind server --embedded`: one tenant, `local`, on a unix socket without a key.

epochs.description: The determinism epochs this server's executors support. New runs start under the last.

mcpUrl.description: The URL MCP clients add as a connector, `{public-url}/mcp`; null without a public URL.

nodes.description: The nodes of the deployment alive now, executors-only nodes included.

oauth.description:
People connect MCP clients with OAuth (`/oauth`): the server has a public URL and a
sign-in. Without it, `/mcp` takes API keys and end users' tokens only.

partitions.description: The partitions of the deployment: 64 by default, 1 for the embedded server.

version.description: The version of the `rewind` binary. A CLI of another version restarts an embedded server.

virtualTime.description: Time is virtual: timers fire as soon as nothing else can advance.

oneOf.description: How its calls authenticate; absent for none.

SessionRequest.description:
`POST /auth/session`: the current state; with `organizationId`, a switch to that
organization.

SetGrant.description:
`PUT /v1/organization/members/{user}/grant`: the member's role and allowed labels. Giving a
role needs every permission of it, and of the member's current role.

SetScriptTitle.description:
`PATCH /v1/scripts/{digest}`: the title and description of a script, for the whole
organization, over those of the comment at its top. The source does not change: a script is
its digest.

example.description: Labels each new issue, and asks for an approval before closing duplicates.
example.title: Triage new GitHub issues

description.description: The description, trimmed: at most 2,000 characters. Absent, `null` or `""`: none.

title.description:
The title, trimmed: 1 to 120 characters. `null` removes the title and the description a
person gave: those of the comment show again.

SignalAccepted.description: `POST /v1/runs/{id}/signals/{name}`: the signal was put in the run's mailbox.

duplicate.description: The `Idempotency-Key` was already used for this run: nothing was added.

SignedTokenClaims.description: The claims of a token the customer signs. Its header names the key: `kid` `rk_…`.

exp.description: Expires at, in seconds since the Unix epoch, at most 30 days after `iat`.

iat.description: Issued at, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

permissions.description: Among those the key may give; [`Permission::TOKEN_DEFAULT`] when absent.

SigningKey.description: One of the organization's signing keys (`archi/04-tools.md`, "Signed calls"): Ed25519.

kid.description:
The key's id, in the `kid` of the JWTs it signs: the first 8 bytes of the SHA-256 of
the public key, in hex.

retiredAt.description: When it stopped signing: it stays published 24 hours longer.

SigningKeyList.description:
`GET /v1/organization/signing-keys`: the current key and those retired less than 24 hours
ago, newest first, and where their public keys are.

issuer.description:
The JWT's issuer, `{public-url}/organizations/{tenant}`: what `verifyRewindCall` is
given as `issuer`.

SkippedOperation.description: An operation of an API that registering left out, and why.

reason.description: Written for the harness developer: `its body is application/xml`.

StartRun.description:
`POST /v1/runs`: starts a run. The script is compiled, checked and type-checked first; a
script that cannot run is refused (`invalid-script`) before any run exists.

With the `Idempotency-Key` header, a request repeated with the same key returns the run the
first one started, instead of starting a second one.

check.description: Type-check the script before starting it. `true` by default.

labels.description:
Run metadata: filters runs, scopes `list_runs`, API keys and webhooks. The script never
sees them.

script.description:
The TypeScript source: a single ES module whose default export is the entry point.
Without it, `workflow` names what the run executes.

secrets.description:
The secrets the run reads, by MCP server or API: `{ "github": "ns/github", "zendesk":
"org/zendesk" }` (`org/<name>`, the organization's; `ns/<name>`, the run's namespace's).
Required for each server the script imports whose `auth` takes a secret; checked against
the caller's rights (`secret-required`). A run of a `workflow` gives none: its version's
are read.

toolset.description: The toolset the script imports from `rewind:tools`. Without one, `rewind:tools` is empty.

traceparent.description:
W3C trace context of the caller (typically the LLM call that wrote the script): the run
appears under it in the caller's trace.

oneOf.description:
The run's TTL: it is cancelled at its deadline. 30 days by default, up to the
deployment's maximum.

Hold the answer until the run ends or is quarantined, or until this long has passed,
however long it is: one request waits, and nothing is asked again meanwhile. Without it,
the answer comes as soon as the run exists.

workflow.description:
Instead of `script` and `toolset`: a run of this workflow, `triage` for its latest version
or `triage@<version>` (12 hex digits at least) or `triage@v12` (its number) for one
version. Its input is checked against the workflow's input schema (`invalid-input`); the
script is not checked again.

StartedBy.description: The run that started a run, and the call that did.

detached.description:
A detached run lives on its own; otherwise the run that started it does not end before
it, and cancels it if it fails or is cancelled.

handle.description: That run's handle; its id once it is erased.

run.description: The id of the run that started it.

StreamEvent.description:
One event of the stream. On the wire, each is a server-sent event whose `event` field is
the `type` below, whose `data` is this JSON object, and, for an entry, whose `id` is the
entry's `idx`.

allOf.description: A committed journal entry. Payload values above 256 KiB are left out.

oneOf.description: A committed journal entry. Payload values above 256 KiB are left out.

The last event of a stream: the run has ended, or, without `follow`, every entry
committed so far was sent.

secret.description: The signing secret, `whsec_…`. Only in the answer to `POST /v1/subscriptions`: keep it.

SuiteTest.description: A test of a version's suite.

TaskGone.description:
The data of a `gone` event: a task handed on this stream no longer waits for its answer. Its
run ended, or its call timed out; an answer sent now is dropped (`task-gone`), and its slot is
free.

token.description: The token the task was handed with.

TaskState.description: The state of a tool task.

TaskStreamEvent.description:
One event of the task stream (`GET /v1/tasks/stream`). On the wire, each is a server-sent
event whose `event` field is `task` or `gone` and whose `data` is this JSON object; events
have no `id`. While it sends nothing else, the server writes a comment line (`:`) at least
every 15 seconds, so that proxies keep the stream open: a client skips comments, and may take
a stream silent for longer as broken. The stream closes once the caller stops authenticating
or no longer holds `tasks:work`, as the change stream does.

oneOf.description: `task`: a task handed to this worker, with its token.
`gone`: a task handed on this stream no longer waits for its answer.

Test.description:
A test: what the run is given (its input, the tools' answers, signals), and what must hold
at the end. It never names its script.

example.name: closes the stale issues once approved

oneOf.description: Where a recorded test comes from; set by recording, refused in a test given inline.

seed.description: The run's seed, 64 lowercase hex digits; the same fixed seed for every test when absent.

signals.description: Sent to the run in order.

start.description: When the run starts, in virtual time; 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z when absent.

TestFrom.description:
A stored test with a new expectation: a model corrects a recorded test without reading its
cassette.

from.description: The digest of the stored test.

TestInput.description:
A test given to `POST /v1/test` or to a save: inline, by the digest of a stored test (one
recorded from a run), or as a stored test with a new expectation.

oneOf.description: The digest of a stored test.

TestOrigin.description: The run a recorded test comes from. The test holds that run's data, and is read like it.

version.description: The workflow version the run executed.

TestProblem.description: Why a test did not pass.

TestRequest.description:
`POST /v1/test`: runs tests in mock mode, in virtual time (`archi/05-testing-and-observability.md`,
"Running tests"). The given tests run against the script; with `workflow`, that version's
suite runs too, and its interface checks every test. This is how a candidate is checked
before it is saved: a corrected script, or the version on a new toolset.

script.description: The TypeScript source. With `workflow`, the version's own when absent.

toolset.description:
The toolset the script imports from `rewind:tools`. With `workflow`, the version's own
when absent.

workflow.description:
A workflow, `triage` (its latest version), `triage@<version>` or `triage@v12`: its suite
runs too.

calls.description: How many times each tool was called.

failures.description: What does not hold, one sentence each, written for a model.

oneOf.description: The run's status; absent for a test that was not run.

trace.description: The LLM trace of the run; empty for a test that was not run.

TestRun.description: `POST /v1/test`: what the tests ran against, and their outcomes.

tests.description: In the order given, then the suite's.

TestSignal.description: A signal sent during a test.

when.description:
When it is sent: `"blocked"` (the default) once the run can go no further without the
outside world; or a duration of virtual time after the start, such as `"2h"`.

TestUpdate.description:
An inherited test replaced: by a whole new test, which takes its name, or by itself with a
new expectation.

TitleSource.description: Where a script's title comes from.

id.description: The SHA-256 of the secret, in hexadecimal (`DELETE /v1/tokens/{id}`).

TokenAlgorithm.description: The algorithm of a token key, from its JWK: Ed25519 (`OKP`), P-256 (`EC`) or RSA.

kid.description: `rk_…`: the `kid` of the tokens it signs.

TokenKind.description: The form of an end user's token.

TokenRequest.description:
`POST /oauth/token`, a form: `authorization_code` (with `code`, `redirect_uri`,
`code_verifier`) or `refresh_token` (with `refresh_token`). The client's id and secret come
in the form or in HTTP Basic authentication.

refresh_token.description: `rewind_rt_…`: used once, it lapses after 30 days unused.

api.description: The API, for an API tool.

policy.description: The policy with its defaults filled in.

server.description: The MCP server, for an MCP tool.

ToolFailure.description: How a tool call failed, as the script sees it (a thrown `ToolError`).

dts.description: The tool's declaration in `rewind-tools.d.ts`, with the types it uses.

prompt.description: The tool's line of the prompt rendering.

ToolPolicy.description:
A tool's policy, pinned in the toolset (`archi/04-tools.md`, "Policies"). Every field is

info.description: The HTTP API /v1 of Rewind: toolsets, scripts, runs, host-tool tasks, webhooks, reading, the organization, access, namespaces and the server; and `/auth`, the dashboard's sign-in. Every request to /v1 carries a Bearer token, an API key (`rewind_sk_…`), a member's access token from `/auth`, or an end user's token (`rewind_nt_…`, or a JWT the customer signed with a key whose `kid` starts with `rk_`), or a person's connection (`rewind_ct_…`), except over the embedded server's unix socket and to the inbound webhook URL. A connection names the organization a request acts in with the header `Rewind-Organization`. What the caller may do is its grant's, or its token's: every operation requires one permission of the catalog (`GET /v1/permissions`), and answers 403 without it. A key or a member names the namespace (the end user) a request acts for with the header `Rewind-Namespace`: required to start a run, check or test a script, it narrows a read to that namespace. An end user's token reaches its own namespace only. `/auth` is for a browser: it reads and writes the cookie `rewind_session`, which /v1 never reads. Errors are `application/problem+json`, with a `detail` written for a model. Fields are camelCase, enumerated values snake_case, times RFC 3339, and durations a number and a unit (`"30s"`, `"1h30m"`) or a number of milliseconds. `/oauth` and `/.well-known` are the OAuth authorization server of people's connections, in OAuth's own formats.

The tasks of the host tools it names (`toolset`, `tools`), as they become ready, among
the runs the caller sees: an end user's token those of its namespace, a key limited to labels those of the
runs carrying them. At most `slots` are in flight on the stream at once. Each event's
`event` field names it and its `data` is a `TaskStreamEvent`: `task`, a task handed with
its token, to answer with `/complete`, `/fail` or `/defer`; `gone`, a task handed on this
stream that no longer waits for its answer. The open stream is the liveness of every task
handed on it: no heartbeat. When it closes, its tasks wait for the grace of their tool
(60 s by default) for a stream opened again with the same `worker`, which keeps them; then
each is handed to another worker with its attempt + 1, or fails with `outcomeUnknown`
under `at_most_once`. A worker opens the stream again after it drops, with a backoff. The
server writes a comment line at least every 15 seconds while it sends nothing else.
